**What type of PR is this?**
/kind cleanup

**What this PR does / why we need it**:
Server-side apply will do type validation. We should no longer be doing this client-side.

Currently, we set `--validate=true` by default for kubectl client-side apply.

For `kubectl apply --server-side`, we should ignore the `--validate` flag.

issue_context.title: SSA: `kubectl apply --server-side` should not client-side validate
issue_context.body: Since some of the objects applied may not be fully valid, we should disable validate by default.
comments: On the other hand, server-side apply doesn't fix the thing that `--validate` was intending to fix (which is mostly to detect misspelled key fields), so I'm not sure why we would disable it. Also, I can't remember why I opened this issue in the first place, is that a real-life example? Let's wait to see more proof of that.
Oh yeah this is related to moving validation server-side. I'm not sure if we got to this yet for SSA and I'm not sure how much of this we actually might do now
I'd like to see evidence that we need this. People, feel free to re-open!

review_comments: should we print an error instead? rather than ignore the flag?

Hm we need to detect if `--validate` is true because it's default or if it's because someone set `--validate=true`, then we would error... I will try this, but I think I remember that cobra might not actually let us do this
